content:
Nigeria’s ambition to expand the use of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) must be matched by a serious commitment to safety. The Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers (NALPGAM), at its recent webinar on operational excellence and compliance, warned that rising consumption alone cannot guarantee a sustainable industry. Every facility must be safe, every operator competent, every process compliant and every customer protected.

The warning is timely. LPG offers households and businesses a cleaner alternative to firewood, charcoal and other polluting fuels, but it is highly flammable. Leaking gas, overfilled cylinders, defective valves, poorly maintained equipment and unsafe storage can turn premises into disaster scenes. Illegal decanting and unauthorised propane blending compound these risks, endangering workers, consumers and neighbouring communities. Such practices must not be treated as commercial shortcuts.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

NALPGAM’s proposed Standard of Operational Excellence, built around safe facilities, trained personnel, compliant processes and consumer protection, deserves support. But a declaration is not enforcement. The association must translate its aspiration into measurable obligations for members, while the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) must sustain inspections, investigate violations and apply sanctions. Operators should maintain equipment, verify cylinder integrity, provide fire and gas-detection systems, and report incidents promptly. Regulators should publish inspection and enforcement data so the public can judge progress.

Technology can strengthen this effort. Smart filling systems, calibrated load cells, flow meters, automated tank gauges and vehicle tracking can improve measurement, trace product movements and expose losses or suspicious transactions. Digital tools, however, are no substitute for trained staff, independent checks and functioning emergency procedures. Small operators may need affordable training, technical guidance and finance for compliant upgrades; such assistance must never become an excuse to relax minimum safety standards.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Safety also has an economic dimension. Accidents destroy lives, property, investment and public confidence. Consumers who fear explosions or suspect short-changing may avoid cooking gas, frustrating efforts to broaden its use. Reliable cylinder traceability, approved exchange arrangements, accurate measurement and clear consumer information can build trust. Government should involve marketers in LPG penetration and cylinder recirculation programmes, while improving supply and distribution infrastructure to make fuel more accessible and affordable.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The stakes extend beyond individual kitchens. Wider adoption of LPG can reduce household exposure to smoke from solid fuels and ease pressure on forests. A safer, better-regulated market can also attract investment, support certified local cylinder manufacturing, create jobs and deepen Nigeria’s energy economy. The national target of five million tonnes of annual LPG consumption by 2030 will mean little if expansion outpaces safety capacity.

Government, regulators and marketers must turn promises into deadlines, audits, transparent reporting and consequences for negligence. Safety must govern every delivery, filling and transaction. Only then can Nigerians embrace gas with confidence, the environment benefit, and the industry become a pillar of economic diversification.

title: Justice, fairness, peace and Nigeria’s 2027 election
excerpt: As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general election, the country stands again at a familiar crossroads: the choice between narrow, sectional calculation and the broader national dem...
description: As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general election, the country stands again at a familiar crossroads: the choice between narrow, sectional calculation and the broader national dem...
content:
As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general election, the country stands again at a familiar crossroads: the choice between narrow, sectional calculation and the broader national demand for justice, fairness and peace. Elections are not merely contests for power. In a plural society such as Nigeria, they are also referendums on whether citizens believe the state belongs to all of them.

Few Nigerian voices expressed this truth more memorably than the late elder statesman and Dan Masanin Kano, Alhaji Yusuf Maitama Sule. In May 2015, Sule led a delegation of the Northern Leaders Forum to congratulate then President-elect Muhammadu Buhari. His counsel on that occasion remains strikingly relevant today.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Sule told Buhari: “With justice, you can rule Nigeria well. Justice is the key.”

It was a simple statement, but one carrying the weight of Nigeria’s history. The country’s recurrent crises—ethnic suspicion, religious tension, electoral violence, insecurity, economic exclusion and the erosion of public trust—are not disconnected accidents. They are symptoms of a deeper disorder: the feeling among many citizens that fairness is selective, opportunity is unequal and power is used to reward loyalty rather than serve the common good.

Sule understood this. “Behind every crisis anywhere in the world is injustice,” he said. And the antidote, he insisted, is “justice.”

That insight should guide every political party, candidate, campaign organisation and voter ahead of 2027. A nation cannot be held together by slogans alone. Neither can it be governed successfully by force, intimidation or the temporary advantage of incumbency. Sule warned: “The world itself can never be governed by force, never by fear, even never by power. In the end, what governs is the mind. What conquers is the spirit and the weapons of governing the mind and conquering the spirit are justice and fair play.”

Nigeria’s 2027 election will therefore test not only the popularity of candidates, but the moral seriousness of the political class.

Justice, in the sense Sule meant it, is broader than court judgments or legal technicalities. It includes fair representation, equitable distribution of public resources, respect for the rule of law, protection of minorities, credible elections and equal treatment before public institutions.

It means that a farmer in Zamfara, a trader in Onitsha, a teacher in Lagos, a fisherman in Bayelsa and a herder in Sokoto should all be able to expect the state to protect their lives, respect their rights and respond to their needs without discrimination.

Sule put it plainly: “If you do justice to all and sundry — and I say all and sundry — because Allah says, ‘If you are going to judge between two people, do justice irrespective of the tribe, religion or even political inclination; justice must be done to whosoever deserves it.’”

That standard is demanding. It rejects the politics of “our turn” when it becomes a cover for exclusion. It also rejects the politics of revenge, where one group’s victory is treated as another group’s defeat. Nigeria needs leaders who can rise above such thinking.

The late Dan Masanin Kano was equally clear that justice must not be selective. “I am not asking you — and I know you will not — to discriminate against any part of Nigeria,” he told Buhari. “But I am asking you to do justice to all parts of Nigeria.”

For political parties preparing for 2027, fairness must begin before the first ballot is cast. It must be visible in candidate selection, zoning arrangements, internal party democracy, campaign financing and the treatment of aspirants.

When parties manipulate primaries, impose candidates, marginalise women and young people, or allow money to determine nomination, they weaken the legitimacy of the eventual winner. A flawed process produces a fragile mandate. And a fragile mandate makes governing harder, especially in a country where citizens are already sceptical of political promises.

Fairness also requires issue-based campaigns. Nigeria’s problems are real: insecurity, unemployment, inflation, poor infrastructure, weak public services, climate pressure on agriculture and widespread poverty. These challenges do not respect ethnicity or religion. Candidates should therefore be judged on their plans to secure communities, create jobs, reform institutions, expand opportunities and restore public confidence.

A campaign built on fear, sectional resentment or religious division may win attention, but it cannot build a nation. Sule’s warning remains urgent: force, fear and power cannot govern the mind or conquer the spirit. Only justice and fair play can.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Sule linked justice directly to peace and development. “Justice will bring about peace,” he said. “Peace and stability are the pre-requisites of development.”

No society develops sustainably in an atmosphere of fear. Investors hesitate where contracts are uncertain and violence is common. Farmers abandon land where insecurity prevails. Young people lose hope where merit is ignored and corruption rewards the connected. Communities retreat into distrust when they believe the state protects some citizens more than others.

Peace is not merely the absence of gunfire. It is the presence of confidence: confidence that elections will count, that courts will be impartial, that public offices will serve the public, and that no region, faith or class will be permanently shut out of opportunity.

The 2027 election offers Nigeria a chance to rebuild that confidence. But it will require more than campaign rhetoric. It will require electoral institutions that are visibly independent, security agencies that act professionally, political actors who accept results peacefully, and citizens who refuse to be used as instruments of violence.

Nigeria does not lack talent, resources or ideas. What it often lacks is the disciplined commitment to justice that turns diversity into strength rather than division. Maitama Sule’s message was not addressed to one president alone. It was addressed to every Nigerian leader, in every generation, and to every citizen who hopes for a better country.

As 2027 approaches, voters should ask hard questions: Which candidate will uphold the rule of law even when it is inconvenient? Which party will distribute opportunity fairly? Which leader will govern for all Nigerians, not merely for those who funded a campaign or share a regional identity?

The answer should not be based on sentiment, ethnicity or fear. It should be based on justice.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Sule’s counsel remains a compass: “With justice, you can rule Nigeria well. Justice is the key.” If Nigeria’s political class embraces that key, the 2027 election can become more than another contest for office. It can become a renewal of the national promise—a step towards a country at peace with itself, fair to all its people, and capable at last of fulfilling its vast potential.

•Ogbeifun wrote in from Lagos.

title: Brazil’s Lula clinches victory over Flavio Bolsonaro to win fourth term
excerpt: Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched election victory against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who tr...

content:
Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched election victory against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who trounced him in the first round.

The leftist icon, who turns 81 on Tuesday, defied all projections to win an unprecedented fourth term at the helm of Latin America’s largest country.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

According to official results, he won 51.75 percentof the votes to 48.25 percent for Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who had entered election day confident with his lead in the polls.

With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump.

After a campaign marred by scandal and mud-slinging, Sunday’s vote plunged into chaos after a last-minute Supreme Court ruling extending voting by two hours, at the request of Lula who said buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting.

Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some parts of the country due to heavy rains, but his camp lashed out at the country-wide extension.

“Either we win. Or we win. Consider yourself warned,” pro-Bolsonaro lawmaker Nikolas Ferreira wrote on X as the votes streamed in.

The bitter campaign laid bare the deep divisions in the country of over 200 million people.

“It’s a disgrace. We’ve never had anything like this in Brazil, and now they’ve come up with the idea of extending the election period by two hours,” said Aurelio Junior, 45, a dentist in Brasilia.

Jacqueline Maria Lima de Franca, 34, a business owner in Rio de Janeiro backing Lula said it was “more than fair…everyone should have the right to vote, and that was being neglected.”

Lula, a defining figure in Brazilian politics over four decades, was blindsided after his first-round defeat to Bolsonaro.

The left swung into action with massive rallies declaring “Never Again Bolsonaro,” where protesters recalled the former president’s chaotic handling of the Covid pandemic, devastation of the Amazon rainforest and cuts to public programs.

Lula also revamped his social media strategy, taking video selfies and even bought his first cellphone, while supporters carried out a feverish campaign to change the minds of family, friends and neighbors, and encourage them to vote after high levels of abstention.

His re-election marks another remarkable comeback for the man who grew up dirt poor in the northeast in a family of illiterate farmers.

Lula, revered for social welfare programs that lifted millions out of poverty, made a dramatic return to office in 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months.

The charges, annulled on procedural grounds, have continued to haunt him.

In his third term he has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but voters complain about the cost of living and a sense of insecurity.

Lula’s social policies became a point of tension as he expanded welfare programs during the campaign.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Brazil needs more time with Lula, primarily because the country is on the verge of falling into the clutches of fascism,” Maria Fernanda Elisbao, a 21-year-old editorial assistant, told AFP.

Lula heads into a fourth term with a country divided, with almost half of the nation voting against him and desperate for change.

“We’re in a deep hole, things are dire. People can barely afford to eat — buying meat is out of the question,” said Tereza Cristina Ramos, a 68-year-old retiree, who voted in Rio de Janeiro.

Already one of the world’s oldest leaders, Lula will be 85 by the end of his new term in 2030.

He will thus have spent 16 years in power, following his first stint as president from 2003 to 2010.

Lula is also facing a hostile Congress dominated by the right.

His options are also constrained by the economic outlook, with growth expected to slow.

He has also come under renewed pressure to confront rampant insecurity in a country plagued by criminal factions that sow terror in working-class neighborhoods.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The president’s campaign leaned heavily on the theme of sovereignty in the face of commercial and diplomatic pressure from Trump’s United States.

Voters must “choose a country where the flag is respected,” he said, his raspy voice more hoarse than ever after a tireless campaign. He accused his rival of wanting to “govern with the American flag.”

content:
The Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has said that the Opebi-Mende Link Bridge is about 80 per cent complete, expressing confidence that the project will be opened to the public before Christmas.

Governor Sanwo-Olu gave the assurance during an inspection of the project, acknowledging that the construction had exceeded the September completion timeline previously announced.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He said his visit to the site was to establish the reasons for the delay and assess the progress of work, stressing that the project’s distinctive architectural design and engineering requirements must not be compromised by the pressure to meet the deadline.

He explained that the bridge’s steel structure was designed to reflect the area’s historical association with cane weaving, thereby preserving its cultural identity.

According to him, the project involves installing more than 300 tonnes of steel at heights of up to 25 metres, making it an unusually demanding engineering undertaking.

The governor said three of the four major steel components, designed to resemble interwoven cane, had been completed, while work was ongoing on the remaining component.

He added that light-emitting diode (LED) installations featuring the colours of Lagos State would enhance the structure and give it an iconic appearance.

Governor Sanwo-Olu added that the state government would not sacrifice engineering quality and public safety for speed, despite the delay.

He said additional activities, including site cleaning, repainting of kerbs, restoration of affected areas and landscaping, would be undertaken before the bridge is opened to the public.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He envisaged the area becoming a destination for recreation, cultural heritage and tourism, adding that its redevelopment would enable residents to appreciate the history and identity of the community.

The governor maintained that the bridge would become a significant infrastructure landmark in Lagos, combining innovation with cultural preservation.

Sanwo-Olu commissioned the construction of the bridge in 2022 to ease congestion in Ikeja and environs.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He said that the bridge, which is part of the ‘legacy project,’ was an innovative solution to the perennial gridlock around Opebi/Mobolaji Bank Anthony Way/Ojota/Mende corridor.

title: Ebola: Lagos Intensifies Surveillance, Reassures Residents Of Preparedness
excerpt: The Lagos State Government has said it is ready to prevent, detect and respond to potential public health threats, amid concerns over the confirmation of Nigeria’s first case of...
description: The Lagos State Government has said it is ready to prevent, detect and respond to potential public health threats, amid concerns over the confirmation of Nigeria’s first case of...
content:
The Lagos State Government has said it is ready to prevent, detect and respond to potential public health threats, amid concerns over the confirmation of Nigeria’s first case of the Bundibugyo virus in the Federal Capital Territory.

It urged residents and visitors not to panic, as the Ministry of Health, through the Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health, is strengthening disease surveillance, risk communication and community engagement, as well as collaboration with agencies at points of entry, including the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), to enhance early detection and response to suspected cases.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The state government said that there is no suspected case of Ebola in Lagos “now”.

It said that as part of its preparedness efforts, it has conducted a strategic engagement and assessment at MMIA with airport management, Port Health Services and other aviation and public health stakeholders.

The engagement, it said, focused on passenger screening, information sharing, infection prevention and control, and coordination of emergency response measures.

The state government further said that the health ministry is also intensifying public enlightenment through educational materials on Ebola, its symptoms, transmission and prevention.

“Ebola Virus Disease is a severe illness that can be fatal. It spreads primarily through direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of an infected person who is showing symptoms, contaminated materials, or the bodies of people who have died from the disease,” it stated.

“Infection may also occur through contact with infected animals. Residents are advised to avoid contact with potentially infectious materials and to rely on verified information rather than rumours or speculation.

“Symptoms may develop between two and 21 days after exposure and include fever, severe weakness, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain. Unexplained bleeding or bruising may occur in some cases.

“As early symptoms can resemble malaria and other common illnesses, residents who become unwell, particularly after possible exposure or travel from an area with active transmission, should seek prompt medical assessment,” it added.

The Lagos State Government further said that anyone with a fever should undergo a malaria rapid diagnostic test before taking antimalarial medicines in line with Lagos State’s fever-management policy.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Where the test is negative, a healthcare professional should assess other possible causes and determine appropriate treatment,” it said. “Residents are also advised to wash their hands regularly, avoid contact with the body fluids of sick persons, refrain from handling potentially contaminated materials and avoid contact with sick or dead wild animals.”

“Travellers arriving in Nigeria, particularly from areas reporting Ebola transmission, are urged to cooperate with Port Health Services and other authorised officials, provide accurate travel and health information when requested, and comply with applicable public health guidance.

“Anyone who develops symptoms during travel or after arrival should promptly notify the appropriate health personnel and seek guidance before visiting a healthcare facility,” it added. “Airlines and airport operators are expected to sustain established public health protocols, while travellers should consult official advisories from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) for current guidance.”

The state government urged anyone who suspects exposure to Ebola, especially following contact with a suspected or confirmed case, to promptly contact public health authorities for guidance before visiting a healthcare facility.

“Suspected cases or relevant exposure concerns in Lagos may be reported through the State’s emergency numbers, 112 or 767, or to the Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health, Lagos State Ministry of Health, on 0802 316 9485,” it added.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“The Lagos State Government will continue to monitor developments, strengthen surveillance and response readiness, coordinate with relevant stakeholders and provide verified updates as necessary. Residents are encouraged to remain calm, practise recommended preventive measures and follow official public health announcements. Early detection and prompt reporting save lives.”

title: 20:24 Inability To Transmit 2023 Presidential Election Results Eroded Trust In INEC — Ex-REC Igini
excerpt: A former resident electoral commissioner, Mike Igini, on Sunday said that the inability of INEC to transmit the results of the 2023 presidential election eroded trust in INEC an...
description: A former resident electoral commissioner, Mike Igini, on Sunday said that the inability of INEC to transmit the results of the 2023 presidential election eroded trust in INEC an...
content:
A former resident electoral commissioner, Mike Igini, on Sunday said that the inability of INEC to transmit the results of the 2023 presidential election eroded trust in INEC and is responsible for the lack of public confidence in the commission.

Igini, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics, said that despite serving as a REC, he still could not explain clearly what constituted the glitch that the electoral umpire claimed was experienced during the election.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He said that while BVAS worked, the failure to transmit one of the results of the three elections held on one day made trust in INEC evaporate.

“Now, in 2023, what worked and what broke public confidence? The BVAS worked. But what broke confidence, which has created a liability and a cloud of distrust that the current leadership is suffering, was the fact that there were three elections, same day; only one could not be transmitted, which was the presidential,” Igini said.

“That was what evaporated public trust and confidence. Even people like us, who put out our integrity to explain to people, to give a clarion call to the Nigerian people, up till date I don’t have a clear explanation of what constituted that glitch.”

The lawyer, however, said that the 2027 elections would be a verdict on whether Nigerians can learn a lesson from what happened in 2023.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Every election is a test, but in 2027, it will be more than a test. It will be a verdict on whether we, as a people, can learn from what has happened,” the former REC said.

He urged Nigerian voters to stay awake, especially on the night of the election when collation happens, to protect their votes.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“But the greatest power of the people, which is unassailable, is that in every polling unit, the people will be more than the polling officials that are going to be compromised,” he said.

title: NDC Unveils Campaign Council, Names Dickson, Obi, Kwankwaso As Members
excerpt: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has constituted its national campaign council for the 2027 general elections.
description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has constituted its national campaign council for the 2027 general elections.
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has constituted its national campaign council for the 2027 general elections.

The list, released on Sunday, has Senator Seriake Dickson as the chairman, while the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, were listed as co-chairman and co-vice chairman of the national campaign caucus, respectively.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Others are Senator Cleopas Zuwoghe as vice chairman, and former secretary to the government of the federation, Babachir Lawal (National Campaign Advisory Council), as a member.

Also on the list are Ikenna Enekweizu, Sidi Abdul, Babatunde Alli, Senator Ovie Omo Agege, Senator Victor Umeh, Ibrahim Abdulkarim (DG, Presidential Campaign), Buba Galadima, Yakubu Ochefu, Mahmud Jahun, Moshood Salvador, Mrs. Dudu Manuga, Victor Ogene, and Muktar Usman.

The list also has a 40-member national campaign advisory council, and 37 state campaign coordinators.

The NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, was named Director of Communication and Media.

A former defence spokesperson, Major General John Enenche (retd.), was named Director of Security and Intelligence.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The party, in a statement announcing the campaign council on its X handle, said,  “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is pleased to announce the constitution of its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections.

“The National Campaign Council will provide strategic leadership, coordinate campaign activities across the country, and drive the mobilisation of Nigerians behind the party’s vision of a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria.

title: Mbappe’s Brace Helps Real Madrid Beat Barcelona In La Liga Clasico
excerpt: Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points.
description: Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points.
content:
Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points.

French superstar Mbappe opened the scoring before the interval and then slotted home late on to inflict Barca’s first domestic defeat of the campaign after Raphinha had equalised for the champions.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Real Madrid remain third, behind Atletico Madrid and Hansi Flick’s Barca, who had won their first nine games before a chastening week.

The Catalans suffered a second straight defeat after losing on Tuesday against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.

Barca had won six of the seven previous Clasicos since the German arrived but were surprisingly subdued against Mourinho’s side.

“In general we didn’t have a great game; in the first half we weren’t ourselves, there were a lot of things we could have done better,” Barcelona midfielder Pedri told DAZN.

“We wanted to win the Clasico in front of our fans, but the season is very long… a league is not won here.”

Los Blancos, without suspended winger Vinicius Junior, won their fifth straight game across all competitions and are finding their footing under veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho.

After two trophyless seasons, Madrid turned back to Mourinho to try and stop Barca’s dominance, and this result will give them hope they are on the right track.

The opening period of the game was cagey, with few opportunities.

Barca defender Pau Cubarsi twice reacted well to shut down Mbappe, while Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella took a rapid liking for Lamine Yamal’s shirt, constantly grabbing at the 19-year-old winger.

Anthony Gordon, playing in his first Clasico since joining Barcelona from Newcastle, backheeled the ball to Raphinha, who fired narrowly wide as Barca threatened.

The hosts were dealt a setback when young defender Xavi Espart pulled up hurt and needed to be replaced by Alejandro Balde before the half-hour mark.

Andriy Lunin, playing in goal for Madrid after Thibaut Courtois pulled out of the squad with flu, saved at his near post from Gordon before the visitors took the lead.

Mbappe scored his 10th league goal of the season and also his easiest, with Barca’s Gerard Martin clearing a cross straight at the Frenchman, who deflected it into the net.

Barca responded by carving out a glorious chance for an equaliser but teenage sensation Yamal, for once, miskicked in front of goal, firing wide when poised to level.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The game opened up, and Yan Diomande came close to doubling Madrid’s lead before half-time, drilling into the side netting.

Martin redeemed himself early in the second half as he held off Jude Bellingham, who could neither beat the defender nor find a free Mbappe.

Raphinha, who had a quiet first half, pulled Barcelona level just after the hour mark.

Pedri fed the Brazilian, La Liga’s top goalscorer with 13, who fired through Bellingham’s legs and Lunin could not keep the shot out.

The Ukrainian goalkeeper did make a superb save to deny Martin at a corner, as Barcelona flowed forward with the wind finally in their sails.

Yamal bent an effort wide with Lunin at full stretch, and Barca substitute Frenkie de Jong had a shot desperately blocked by Dean Huijsen.

There was a sting in the tail for the Catalans, though as substitute Gabriel Jesus lost possession and Madrid raced through on goal.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Eduardo Camavinga beat Cubarsi and unselfishly cut the ball back for Mbappe to tuck home his second of the night into an empty net with Joan Garcia drawn out of position.

title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab
excerpt: The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.
description: The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.
content:
The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.

As part of Wednesday's Budget, the government will commit £100m to establishing the new, "world first" institute with the support of leading AI firms.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The chancellor will also pledge millions of pounds in spending across a range of initiatives aimed at shoring up the UK's ability to respond to evolving cyber, biological and AI-enabled threats.

"AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school, and every aspect of our economy can benefit," John Healey said.

"I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI.

"One that doesn't leave workers behind and defends our national interest, while ensuring the benefits of AI-enabled growth are felt right across the country."

The full details about the role and remit of the new lab are yet to emerge.

But the AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said it would be a "major new global institution" that brings together "world-leading scientific expertise" to ensure the UK can safeguard its citizens and goals as AI develops.

"That means staying ahead of emerging threats, from cyber attacks to biological risks, while building more of the critical technology our security depends on," he said.

"By backing British science, advanced chips and our own AI companies, we can strengthen our national security, rebuild Britain's industrial strength and create good, skilled jobs across the country."

The AI Biosecurity Lab's creation will also be supported by leading AI developers, with OpenAI and Anthropic providing £200m worth of AI model credits that can be spent on the use of their models.

What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

Don't leave AI to tech bros and oligarchs, UK's AI minister says

The Chancellor's plans to boost AI spending will also see an additional £120m committed to the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI).

Established by the former Conservative government in 2023, the lab evaluates the risks of the most advanced and powerful models - and has been championed for its role in helping build a collaborative and open approach to AI testing.

The additional funding announced by the Chancellor will aim to help ensure the lab can continue its efforts and work, particularly amid growing calls for technical standards and guardrails for AI development.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

It will come alongside a £60m investment in what it coined a "National Cyber Shield" which it said would use agentic AI to boost cyber-defences, and £70m funding towards a National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability (NERV) Centre.

This, it said, would harness AI tools to detect cyber vulnerabilities across the UK's critical infrastructure and economy.

It comes after the UK government revealed it was among organisations around the world to have taken some sites offline as a precaution after critical flaws were surfaced in a popular programming language.

Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side scripting language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks.

There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far.

But experts have warned that the incident shows how quickly and easily bugs which have lain long dormant may be surfaced - and potentially exploited - using AI.

content:
Tech tycoon Elon Musk accused Ukraine on Saturday of violating Starlink’s terms of service by using it for “drone strikes to kill people,” after tension between Washington and Kyiv over disruptions to the SpaceX-made network crucial to the Ukrainian army’s operations.

“Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people,” Musk wrote in a post on X, but added that the loophole was closed last week.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“Starlink’s terms have remained consistent as a civilian system, not a means of killing. Violation of those terms will result in end of service,” he wrote in another post.

He added that Starlink remained “critical to the defence of Ukraine, as it is the only system that cannot be jammed or blown up, at least for now. Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately.”

While Musk has shifted stance on Ukraine many times since Russia’s invasion in 2022, he has insisted that any disruption was the responsibility of the US government, not SpaceX.

Kyiv relies on the civilian Starlink satellite communications system and the military-grade Starshield version as it tries to defend itself from Russian missile and drone attacks.

“Monitoring systems are recording a recovery in the speed of Starlink/Starshield. We are registering a speed of more than 400 km/h, the connection is stable,” Defence Minister Yevgeniy Khmara said in a statement on Saturday.

“This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications,” he added.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Right now, the speed is what we need. The restoration began during the night,” he said on social media.

“This is very important; it’s significant for our frontline logistics, for protecting Ukraine” from rocket-powered drones, he stressed.

The satellite network has been at the centre of a row between Ukraine and the United States.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Zelensky had accused Washington of helping Russia by failing to warn Kyiv of incoming missile strikes and hobbling its military response by throttling Starlink’s speed.

Khmara credited Zelensky’s “firm stance” on the issue, judging that it was “bearing fruit.”

title: Save our ancestral lands, Ogun communities beg Abiodun
excerpt: Residents of Fere and Oniporogun communities in Orile-Mo, Obafemi Owode Local Government Area of Ogun State, have appealed to Governor Dapo Abiodun to intervene in an alleged la...
description: Residents of Fere and Oniporogun communities in Orile-Mo, Obafemi Owode Local Government Area of Ogun State, have appealed to Governor Dapo Abiodun to intervene in an alleged la...
content:
Residents of Fere and Oniporogun communities in Orile-Mo, Obafemi Owode Local Government Area of Ogun State, have appealed to Governor Dapo Abiodun to intervene in an alleged land allocation to Chinese investors, noting that the development could render hundreds of families homeless and destroy their ancestral heritage.

The residents made the appeal during a protest on Saturday at the disputed site, alleging that bulldozers and security personnel had been deployed to commence operations on land where homes and other properties had already been developed.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

They urged the state government to halt further activities on the land and convene an urgent meeting with community leaders and other stakeholders to resolve the dispute, insisting that industrial development should not come at the expense of residents’ homes, investments and livelihoods.

The Baale of Fere, Chief Okesola Alani, said residents had been engaging the government since 2017 over the need for an extension of the village, lamenting that the matter remained unresolved.

He explained that residents had made collective efforts to develop the area, including providing electricity through communal contributions, while many had invested their savings in acquiring land and building houses.

Alani said, “We are not fighting the government for development. We want the community to be developed; we want industries. But the industry we are bringing should not be at the expense of the community. We don’t have any place to go.”

The traditional ruler alleged that community leaders were not consulted before the disputed land allocation, claiming that security operatives and heavy-duty equipment were brought to the area without prior engagement with the residents.

“Before any government can allocate, they have to contact the leader of the village, the Baale. None of us was contacted. They just came with police, caterpillars and other equipment and started bulldozing our land,” he alleged.

He maintained that sufficient land was available for industrial development without encroaching on existing homes, appealing to Abiodun to protect the residents and ensure that they could coexist peacefully with investors.

“We are begging Governor Dapo Abiodun. I know he is an achiever and he is making progress, but please, Dapo and your government, remember us. We are human beings,” Alani said.

The Baale also said he had obtained traditional recognition from the Olu of Orile-Mo, the Ologbon of Imo and the Alake of Egbaland, describing himself as the recognised traditional head of the community.

Similarly, the Acting Chairman of the Community Development Association of Oniporogun and Fere communities, Salau Hamid, appealed to the government to consider the plight of residents who had struggled to build homes despite the prevailing economic hardship.

“It is saddening that we are trying, even though the economy is bad, to make sure that we have our buildings, and we found out that the Chinese are taking over. We don’t know how it came to play,” Hamid said.

He claimed that more than 300 residents had houses either completed or under construction in the affected communities, urging the government to consider the financial and emotional consequences of displacing them.

“We want development, yes, but this is not the kind of development we are looking at. We want to exist and co-exist with the Chinese, but they can always get properties elsewhere,” he added.

Hamid urged the government to suspend any demolition of residents’ properties pending consultations, noting that many affected landlords had obtained documents relating to their land and buildings.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Another resident and landlord, Mr Ipadeola Afeez, appealed to the state and Federal Governments to intervene before residents lost their properties, alleging that some individuals were exploiting the proposed Chinese investment to take over land belonging to community members.

Afeez said several landlords had complied with government requirements by obtaining survey plans, ratification documents and assessments, while some had also secured Certificates of Occupancy.

“We don’t understand what has happened. We have done all the necessary documents that government said we should do,” he said.

He called on the state government to rescue residents from what he described as the activities of land grabbers.

“Please and please, we are Nigerians. We have nowhere to go. We are appealing to the state government to come and rescue us from all these land grabbers,” Afeez said.

He further alleged that the proposed development covered parts of the communities where some residents had buried their ancestors, describing the situation as a threat to both their homes and ancestral heritage.

A resident and businesswoman, Mrs Komaya Racheal, also appealed to the state government to protect the residents and their properties.

“Please consider us, government. Please, we are seeking mercy. Nothing much. We are appealing to Governor Dapo Abiodun to help us secure our land,” she said.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The residents urged the Ogun State Government to urgently convene a meeting involving traditional leaders, landlords, the Community Development Association and other relevant stakeholders to resolve the dispute.

They maintained that industrial development could proceed without destroying existing homes or displacing families, calling on the government to ensure that the rights and interests of affected residents were considered in any decision concerning the disputed land.

title: Nigerian businesses need more than loans to grow — Oyedele
excerpt: The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigerian businesses require more than conventional loans to expand, stressing the need ...
description: The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigerian businesses require more than conventional loans to expand, stressing the need ...
content:
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigerian businesses require more than conventional loans to expand, stressing the need for patient capital, experienced investors and institutional support to overcome persistent barriers to growth.

Oyedele said this on Saturday in Abuja at the fourth edition of the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority Prize for Innovation, where seven startups received awards valued at $277,000.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Represented by his Special Adviser on Finance and Investment, Marie Ukpere, the minister said access to credit alone could not address the structural challenges confronting entrepreneurs.

“We also recognise that high-potential businesses often require more than conventional credit. They need patient capital, experienced investment partners, and networks that can help them enter new markets and achieve scale,” he said.

He noted that although small and medium-sized enterprises sustained millions of livelihoods and provided employment across the country, many struggled to expand because of inadequate financing, technical capacity and institutional backing.

“Too many promising businesses struggle to grow because they cannot access financing, skills, or institutional support they need to succeed,” Oyedele added.

According to him, Nigeria’s ambition to build a $1tn economy depends significantly on transforming small businesses into medium-sized enterprises and eventually large companies capable of competing internationally.

He identified the Development Bank of Nigeria and the National Credit Guarantee Company as institutions supporting access to business financing, explaining that the latter was designed to reduce lending risks and encourage banks to extend credit to SMEs and manufacturers.

Oyedele also highlighted the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation’s efforts to strengthen household purchasing power and domestic demand.

He cited the $618m Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises programme as another intervention supporting young entrepreneurs through financing, skills development and business assistance.

The minister disclosed that the NSIA was anchoring venture capital funds to attract institutional investment into Nigerian enterprises and developing an impact innovation fund with the Japan International Cooperation Agency, with British International Investment expressing interest in participating.

He said the proposed fund would support commercially viable businesses addressing economic and development challenges.

“The real measure of your success will not be the prize you receive today. It will be the businesses you go on to build afterwards,” Oyedele told the finalists.

Earlier, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the NSIA, Aminu Umar-Sadiq, disclosed that the 12 finalists emerged from more than 6,000 applications following five stages of screening and business development activities.

Speaking further during an interview with journalists, Umar-Sadiq explained that the competition formed part of the authority’s investment strategy to support entrepreneurs alongside its infrastructure financing activities.

He said the programme focused on healthcare, manufacturing and food systems this year because of their potential to generate employment, develop skills and improve productivity.

The NSIA boss added that all 12 finalists would participate in a six-week learning programme at Lagos Business School, while strategic partners would provide additional opportunities for financing and business development.

He explained that the authority monitored its investments by working with beneficiary companies to improve corporate governance, strengthen management and expand demand for their products.

“When the equity injection goes into these companies, we work very closely with the management teams to enhance their value proposition, strengthen their governance and broaden the demand for their products,” he said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Citing previous winners, including Money Africa and Sycamore, Umar-Sadiq maintained that the impact of startup investments should be assessed over approximately five years rather than expecting immediate results.

Also speaking, the National Coordinator of the Presidential Unlocking Healthcare Value Chain Initiative, Dr Abdu Mukhtar, identified healthcare as a major investment opportunity, estimating Nigeria’s addressable healthcare market at $20bn.

“We estimate that across the healthcare value chain, the addressable market is about $20bn. There are already about 250,000 SMEs in healthcare, according to the IFC,” he said.

Mukhtar identified pharmaceutical manufacturing, medical devices, clinical research, telemedicine and healthcare logistics as areas offering opportunities for entrepreneurs.

The founder and Chief Executive Officer of ReelFruit and lead judge of the competition, Affiong Williams, said her company had raised more than $7m over 14 years, attributing its ability to attract investment to preparation, credibility and resilience.

She urged entrepreneurs to understand customer demand, build strong networks and remain focused despite economic instability.

Similarly, Cascador Founder and Director, Dave DeLucia, argued that preparing businesses to attract investment was as important as providing capital.

“Capital readiness is just as important or more than the capital itself,” he said, adding that entrepreneurs outside Lagos often required greater institutional support.

At the competition, Come Again Foods emerged as the overall winner, receiving a combined $105,000 prize, while Protein Kapital and InstantRad finished second and third, securing $70,000 and $50,000, respectively.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Other beneficiaries included Eight Medical, Uwana Energy, Tryctor and Smartei Agri Tech.

The NSIA said the $277,000 award package comprised $220,000 from the authority, $45,000 from Cascador and $12,000 from Wema Bank, with additional opportunities for business development and investment support.

excerpt: Old students of Imade College, Owo, Ondo State, under the auspices of the Imade College Old Students Association, have appealed to the state government to address the shortage o...
description: Old students of Imade College, Owo, Ondo State, under the auspices of the Imade College Old Students Association, have appealed to the state government to address the shortage o...
content:
Old students of Imade College, Owo, Ondo State, under the auspices of the Imade College Old Students Association, have appealed to the state government to address the shortage of teachers in the school.

The association said it had been hiring and paying ad hoc teachers to bridge the staffing gap and prevent students from suffering the consequences of inadequate teaching personnel.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The Chairman of the Planning Committee for the school’s 80th anniversary, Yinka Akinola, disclosed this on Saturday at the grand finale of the anniversary celebration held at the school.

Akinola said the old students had spent about N11m this year to engage ad hoc teachers, noting that the money could have been used for infrastructural development if there had been enough teachers in the school.

He said, “The major problem we are facing in this school is staffing. This year alone, the old students have spent about N11m employing ad hoc teachers. I am a member of the endowment committee. We pay them reasonably well, even above the minimum wage, to ensure that they can support themselves and remain committed to their work.

“The N11m we have spent on these teachers could have been channelled towards upgrading facilities in the college. Instead, we have to use the money to address the shortage of teachers.”

Akinola also disclosed that IMACOSA had spent over N200m on projects to improve facilities at the school as part of activities marking its 80th anniversary.

He said about 10 projects had been inaugurated, including classrooms, laboratories, accommodation facilities, three-bedroom flats and public toilets.

Commending the National President of the Imade College Owo Old Students Association Worldwide, Ambassador Godson Echegile, Akinola said he was one of the major contributors to the projects, having spent over N100m on the school this year alone.

He noted that some of the projects were executed by individuals and different sets of alumni as part of efforts to give back to the institution.

Akinola said the interventions were aimed at improving the learning environment and making students more comfortable, but stressed that inadequate teaching staff remained a major challenge.

Akinola, who left the college in 1971 when it had about 300 students, said the school’s population had grown considerably, putting existing facilities under pressure and making the alumni interventions necessary.

He, however, acknowledged improvements in some facilities, including computer laboratories, which were not available during his time at the school.

Also speaking, the Vice-President of IMACOSA Worldwide, Surveyor Felix Ajibade, said the association had employed 29 ad hoc teachers, each paid N70,000 monthly, to prevent students from suffering the consequences of the teacher shortage.

Ajibade appealed to the government to provide more teachers, drivers and security personnel, noting that the college had three vehicles but no drivers.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He added that the institution needed security personnel to protect its premises during the day and at night.

He said, “We have a shortage of teachers. That is why IMACOSA decided to employ 29 ad hoc teachers, whom we pay N70,000 each every month. Otherwise, the students would suffer. The government has not provided enough teachers.

“We also do not have drivers, despite having three vehicles. It is not appropriate for teachers to be driving the school buses. A lawyer will tell you that it is illegal. We need to have drivers in place.

“Furthermore, this college is large, and we need security personnel to protect it, not only during the day but also at night. We have appealed to the government to assist us in these areas. We need more teachers, drivers and security personnel.”

content:
The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project has sued the Federal Government at the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice over alleged diversion, irregular expenditure and failure to account for N78.8bn allocated to cash-transfer and social-protection programmes.

SERAP, in a statement released by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare, on Sunday, said the allegations involved the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, the National Cash Transfer Office and the National Social Safety Nets Coordinating Office.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The allegations were documented in the Auditor-General of the Federation’s 2024 Annual Report, published on August 7, 2026.

According to the report, the findings covered various periods between January 2023 and December 31, 2024.

In the suit, marked ECW/CCJ/APP/42/26 and filed last week, SERAP is seeking a declaration that the government’s failure to account for the funds violates Nigeria’s international human rights obligations.

The organisation is also asking the court to order the government to provide a comprehensive account of the questioned funds, investigate the alleged irregularities, recover any money improperly spent or diverted where established, and strengthen financial oversight of social-protection programmes.

SERAP argued that the alleged financial irregularities could undermine the rights of vulnerable Nigerians to social security and an adequate standard of living, including access to food, clothing and housing.

The statement party read, “The funds were intended to benefit over 3.2 million households across 35 states, whose access to financial assistance has been affected by the allegations made by the Auditor-General.”

The suit, filed by SERAP’s lawyers, Kolawole Oluwadare and Kehinde Oyewumi, stated that the government’s failure to investigate the allegations and recover any improperly spent funds violated its obligations to protect vulnerable households.

“The failure to investigate the N78.8 billion cash-transfer scandal, account for the questioned funds and recover any unlawfully spent amounts violates Nigeria’s obligations to protect the human rights of vulnerable households,” the suit partly read.

The organisation said it instituted the case to protect affected households and ensure accountability for public funds allocated for their benefit.

“SERAP brings this public-interest case to protect the interests of affected households and ensure accountability for public funds allocated for their benefit,” it stated.

The organisation maintained that cash-transfer programmes could help address extreme poverty and enable vulnerable people to meet their basic needs, but argued that the government had a duty to ensure the funds were properly managed.

“The right to social security cannot be effectively realised merely by establishing a formal cash-transfer programme where the State fails to maintain reasonable systems for identifying beneficiaries, maintaining records, reconciling disbursements, monitoring expenditure, investigating irregularities and remedying losses,” the statement further stated.

According to SERAP, the Auditor-General questioned approximately N33.751bn reportedly transferred to more than 3.2 million households across 35 states in 2023, noting that adequate records to verify the payments and reconcile beneficiary records were not provided.

The report also identified N36.744bn in payments allegedly made without prepayment audits, N4.616bn in unsupported expenditures, N350.182m for enrolment, N89.511m for store purchases and N17.422m in diesel advances.

SERAP said the suit was brought under Article 9(4) of the ECOWAS Court Protocol to protect affected households and ensure accountability for public funds intended for social protection.

“The issue is whether the government has discharged its obligations under applicable human-rights treaties to safeguard resources allocated for social protection, investigate documented financial irregularities, provide effective remedies and ensure that those resources are applied for their intended purposes,” it stated.

The organisation also cited the constitutional responsibility of the Auditor-General to audit and report on the public accounts of the Federation and the offices and agencies of the Federal Government, describing the findings in the annual report as important official records of public expenditure.

It relied on Articles 1 and 2 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, arguing that the government had obligations to give effect to protected rights and ensure that failures in administering social-protection programmes did not result in discriminatory exclusion or unequal access to benefits.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“The Nigerian government has the obligation to take effective measures to prevent and address corruption and related misuse of public resources. The government has failed to take appropriate measures in response to the allegations made by the Auditor-General”, the statement added.

SERAP said it had previously urged President Bola Tinubu and relevant authorities to account for the questioned funds, publish audit records, investigate irregular expenditures, recover any funds unlawfully spent or diverted and take appropriate action against those responsible.

Following the publication of the Auditor-General’s report, the organisation issued a public statement and sent a letter dated September 5, 2026, requesting action on the findings. It also sought payment and beneficiary records, verification documents and an explanation for the missing REMITA records.

“The deadline given to the government to address the Auditor-General’s findings had elapsed without adequate action,” it stated.

The organisation further cited Articles 1 and 21 of the African Charter, alongside Article 9 of the United Nations Convention against Corruption, as requiring effective measures to protect rights and resources, promote transparent public financial management, investigate irregularities and recover public funds where losses or improper expenditure were established.

SERAP also relied on the works of legal scholar Kolawole Olaniyan, including Corruption and Human Rights Law in Africa, published by Hart Publishing in 2014, and Ownership of Proceeds of Corruption in International Law, published by Oxford University Press in 2023. It said the publications provided persuasive academic authority on corruption’s effects on human rights, public resources, accountability and international legal remedies.

“SERAP accordingly submits that the Auditor-General’s findings cannot be treated merely as administrative irregularities where public funds allocated for social protection may have been lost, improperly spent or left unaccounted for, and the government fails to take effective corrective action,” the statement added.

SERAP is asking the court to direct the government to conduct an independent, prompt and effective investigation into the identified irregularities, recover public funds improperly spent, diverted or lost where established, and take appropriate legal or administrative action against those found responsible, in accordance with due process.

It also wants the government to strengthen financial accountability, beneficiary verification, auditing, reconciliation and oversight mechanisms to prevent a recurrence of the alleged irregularities and ensure that eligible vulnerable households receive their intended benefits.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The organisation is further seeking an order restraining the government from administering or disbursing cash-transfer and social-protection funds without adequate accountability and oversight mechanisms, as well as appropriate remedies for any established adverse effects on beneficiaries’ protected rights.

No date has been fixed for the hearing of the suit.

content:
The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has sued the Federal Government at the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice over alleged financial irregularities involving more than ₦78.8 billion allocated to cash-transfer and social protection programmes.

The organisation said the allegations involved the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, the National Cash Transfer Office (NCTO) and the National Social Safety Nets Coordinating Office (NASSCO).

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

According to SERAP, the issues were documented in the Auditor-General of the Federation’s 2024 Annual Report, published on August 7, 2026, covering various periods between January 2023 and December 31, 2024.

In the suit, numbered ECW/CCJ/APP/42/26 and filed last week, SERAP is asking the court to declare that the government’s alleged failure to account for the funds allocated to federal cash-transfer and social protection programmes violates Nigeria’s international human rights obligations.

The organisation is also seeking an order directing the government to provide a comprehensive and verifiable account of the questioned funds, including payment records, beneficiary details, verification documents and financial reconciliation records.

SERAP further wants the court to order an independent investigation into the alleged irregularities, the recovery of any public funds found to have been improperly spent or diverted, and appropriate legal or administrative action against anyone found responsible, subject to due process.

According to the organisation, the Auditor-General’s report questioned approximately ₦33.751 billion reportedly transferred to more than 3.2 million households across 35 states in 2023, citing inadequate records to verify payments and reconcile beneficiary information.

The report also identified ₦36.744 billion in payments allegedly made without prepayment audits and ₦4.616 billion in unsupported expenditure.

Other questioned payments included ₦350.182 million for enrolment, ₦89.511 million for store purchases and ₦17.422 million in diesel advances, SERAP said, citing the audit report.

The organisation argued that the alleged financial irregularities raised concerns about whether the funds were properly managed and whether intended beneficiaries received the assistance meant to support vulnerable households.

In its application, SERAP maintained that the government’s responsibility to protect human rights extended to the proper management of public resources allocated to social protection programmes.

It argued that failures to verify beneficiaries, maintain accurate records, reconcile disbursements, investigate irregularities and recover misused funds could undermine the rights to social security and an adequate standard of living, including access to food, clothing and housing.

“The failure to investigate the ₦78.8 billion cash-transfer scandal, account for the questioned funds and recover any unlawfully spent amounts violates Nigeria’s obligations to protect the human rights of vulnerable households,” the organisation said in its court filing.

SERAP said the case was brought in the public interest to protect affected households and promote accountability for public funds allocated to social protection.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The organisation also argued that the alleged failures could affect millions of Nigerians who depend on cash-transfer programmes to meet basic needs, particularly people living in poverty.

The suit was filed on behalf of SERAP by its lawyers, Kolawole Oluwadare and Kehinde Oyewumi, under Article 9(4) of the ECOWAS Court Protocol.

SERAP said it had previously urged President Bola Tinubu and relevant authorities, in a letter dated September 5, 2026, to account for the questioned funds, publish relevant audit records, investigate the expenditure and recover any money found to have been unlawfully spent or diverted.

It also requested payment and beneficiary records, verification documents and explanations regarding missing REMITA records.

According to the organisation, the deadline it gave the government to address the audit findings had elapsed without adequate action.

SERAP is asking the court to direct the government to strengthen financial accountability, auditing, beneficiary verification and oversight mechanisms to prevent similar irregularities in future cash-transfer and social protection programmes.

It also wants measures put in place to ensure eligible vulnerable individuals and households receive the benefits intended for them and that any established adverse effects on their rights are appropriately addressed.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The organisation is relying on provisions of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights and the United Nations Convention against Corruption in arguing that governments have obligations to protect public resources, ensure transparent financial management and investigate suspected misuse of public funds.

No date has been fixed for the hearing of the suit.

content:
The Katsina State Government says community hunters foiled a planned mass kidnapping in Gidan Wawo village, Kakumi Ward, Bakori Local Government Area, following a gun battle with suspected bandits that left 14 of the attackers dead.

According to the government, intelligence received at about 1:28 a.m. on Friday indicated that 26 heavily armed bandits riding on 13 motorcycles were heading towards Dawan Laila Forest ahead of planned attacks on neighbouring communities.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

They were reportedly led by a suspected kingpin, Isiya Kwashen Garwa.

Security agencies subsequently placed all operational assets in Bakori Local Government Area on high alert, disrupting the planned abduction.

However, at about 1:31 p.m. the same day, the bandits attacked a private vehicle conveying four passengers from Kakumi Ward to Illela Market in Sokoto State and set it ablaze, trapping the occupants.

Community hunters from Gidan Wawo were mobilised and engaged the fleeing attackers in a gun battle, killing 14 suspected bandits and rescuing three passengers alive.

The incident claimed the lives of two people: 29-year-old community hunter Mohammed Ibrahim Jidda, who was killed while defending the community, and 50-year-old traveller Jamilu Lawal, the fourth passenger, who died from burns sustained in the vehicle fire.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Another hunter, 25-year-old Usman Sunday, sustained minor gunshot injuries and is receiving medical treatment.

The government said intelligence reports indicated possible reprisal following the bandits’ losses. It added that countermeasures had been activated in collaboration with security agencies to prevent further threats.

Commending the security personnel and community hunters for their intervention, the government said their actions prevented what could have been a devastating mass kidnapping.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

In a statement signed by the Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Dr Nasir Mu’azu Danmusa, the government urged residents to remain calm and vigilant and to continue providing timely, credible intelligence to security agencies. It also reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives and property across the state.

Desmond Sunday Stephen NDYN Commends His Investment in Youths, Women and Human Capital Development The National Delta Youths Network (NDYN) has unanimously passed a Vote of Confidence on Hon. Desmond Sunday Stephen, a distinguished son of Okrika, Rivers State, in recognition of his contributions to human capital development and his continued commitment to the advancement of youths, women and students across the Niger Delta. The commendation was contained in a statement issued by the National President of NDYN, Hon. Comrade Scott Uyiosasere Ogunseri, who described Hon. Desmond has distinguished himself through sustained investments in people and communities, particularly through initiatives focused on education, entrepreneurship and youth empowerment. Supporting Students and Empowering Communities NDYN highlighted several areas of Hon. Desmond's intervention, including scholarships for indigent students, business grants for women and youths, as well as various empowerment initiatives designed to improve livelihoods and create opportunities for people across communities. Comrade Scott noted that such interventions demonstrate a commitment to leadership that goes beyond words and places tangible impact at the centre of public service. «“In a time when many have abandoned our people, Hon. Desmond Sunday Stephen has chosen to stand with women, youths and students. He is proof that leadership is about service. He is Okrika’s pride and Niger Delta’s hope,” Comrade Scott stated.» NDYN Reaffirms Support The National Delta Youths Network expressed appreciation to Hon. Desmond for his consistent support for young people, women and students, while reaffirming the organisation's solidarity with his efforts toward human capital development. NDYN said it remains committed to recognising and supporting individuals whose contributions positively affect the lives of people across the Niger Delta. The organisation concluded by celebrating Hon. Desmond Sunday Stephen for his contributions and expressing gratitude for his continued efforts toward empowering the next generation. Signed: Hon. Comr. Scott Ogunseri National President, National Delta Youths Network (NDYN) One Voice. One People. One Destiny.

Niger Delta Youth Network Unveils National Executive Council


Niger Delta, Nigeria: The Niger Delta Youth Network (NDYN) has unveiled its National Executive Council, comprising young leaders entrusted with the responsibility of advancing the network’s vision, mission, unity, development and collective interests of youths across the Niger Delta region.

The newly constituted National Executive Council is expected to provide strategic leadership and direction as the organization works towards strengthening youth participation in development, promoting peace and unity, and creating opportunities for young people across the region.

Operating under the core values of CONNECT • EMPOWER • TRANSFORM, the NDYN leadership is committed to promoting youth leadership, peacebuilding, entrepreneurship, education, innovation, inclusion, responsible citizenship and sustainable development.

National Executive Council

The National Executive Council comprises the following officers:

1. National President: Comrade Scott Uyiosasere Ogunseri
2. National Vice President (Administration): Comrade Solomon Imafidon
3. National Secretary: Comrade Isoboye Edwin
4. Vice President (West): Comrade Dauda Femiola John
5. Vice President (East): Comrade Chidebere Godspel
6. Vice President (North): Comrade Sandra
7. Assistant Secretary: Comrade Stanley Osaghae

13. Director of Technology & Innovation I: Comrade Osahon Chris Odia
14. Director of Technology & Innovation II: Comrade Adams Aimienoho
15. Director of Stakeholder Engagement: Comrade Ominidougha Pere-Egbewei Stanley
16. Director of Entrepreneurship: Comrade Jite-Eda God’sMajesty
17. Director of Welfare: Comrade Happiness Bibo Adams
18. Director of Women Affairs: Comrade Sandra Osariemen
19. Director of Special Duties II: Comrade Collins Ogieva Osagie
20. Director of Gender Affairs: Comrade Faith Ogaga
21. Director of Students Affairs: Comrade Assor Favour
22. Director of Security, Peace & Conflict Resolution I: Comrade John Uwanogho
23. Director of Security, Peace & Conflict Resolution II: Comrade Aideyan Louis Owamamwen
24. Director of Mobilization I: Comrade Henry Chikodi Dennar
25. Director of Mobilization II: Comrade Yenne Ebobrah Dennis
26. Director of Mobilization III: Comrade Efeyi
27. Director of Mobilization IV: Comrade Samuel Feghaowei Johnny
28. Director of Mobilization V: Comrade Oghogho Ayo Obaseki
29. Director General, Media & Communication: Comrade Akpa Gideon Ifeanyi
30. Director of Media & Communication II: Comrade Udofia Gideon Sampson
31. Director of Media & Communication III: Comrade Fidelis Emmanuel Sibe

A New Commitment to Niger Delta Youths

According to the network, the National Executive Council will work collectively to strengthen youth engagement and create an environment where young people can contribute meaningfully to the social and economic development of the Niger Delta.

The leadership's focus areas include youth empowerment, entrepreneurship, education, technology and innovation, peace and conflict resolution, stakeholder engagement, gender inclusion, student affairs and sustainable development.

With a broad representation across different areas of youth development and advocacy, the council is expected to leverage collaboration and collective action in addressing issues affecting young people in the region.

Building a Stronger Niger Delta

The NDYN says its ultimate goal is to build a stronger, more united and prosperous Niger Delta where young people are empowered to become leaders, entrepreneurs, innovators and nation builders.

The network's message to Niger Delta youths is clear:

The National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) has approved 23 new academic programmes for Federal Polytechnic Ukana, Akwa Ibom State, beginning from the 2026/2027 academic session.


The development is a major milestone for the institution as it expands its academic offerings across engineering, technology, sciences, business, security and other professional fields.

2. ND Artificial Intelligence
3. ND Estate Management and Valuation
4. ND Building Technology
5. ND Petroleum Marketing & Business Studies

A Major Expansion for the Polytechnic

The newly approved programmes significantly broaden the range of courses available to students at Federal Polytechnic Ukana.

The approval also strengthens the Polytechnic's offerings in engineering, science laboratory technology, business management, accounting, environmental studies and other technical disciplines.

The new programmes are expected to commence with the 2026/2027 academic session, providing prospective students with more options when applying to the institution.

title: Nene Essien: Leading the Charge Through the NAUS Campus Tour Across Akwa Ibom State
excerpt: In a landscape where student leadership is often reduced to titles and visibility, Nene Essien, popularly known as Peculiar Oluwa, is positioning herself differently.
